findings.failure: Read sharing is now engine-owned (request-owned FrontierCache, Arc rows, Weak entries) but not enforced: frontiers::service::prepare is pub(crate), so any execution-crate caller can read the providers directly and bypass the cache. The only guarantee is that today's single caller goes through FrontierCache::shared; a compliant call site is not a boundary.
findings.required_enforcement: Narrow prepare to the cache (pub(in ...frontiers) called only from FrontierCache::shared, or make the cache the sole constructor of PreparedFrontiers), with a compile-fail probe in boundary_contract that a file_dag caller cannot reach prepare and a positive probe through ExecutionRequest::prepare_frontiers.

findings.failure: The 28-method census is generated by methods! (variants cannot be missing from ALL: fixed), but the trait set is hand-selected: ObservationPublication is a public entry trait implemented by ObservationStage (core cross_file/coordinator.rs imports it) whose install(rule, ..) and restore_frontiers(.., inapplicable: &[InapplicableFiles], ..) take per-rule submissions and are not in implements_every_entry_trait, so an incomplete/extra/undeclared root or a wrong-length inapplicable slice on those routes has no control. Earlier hole (c) remains: a new trait method can call witness(Method::<existing>) and its control never runs; nothing checks one variant per method.
findings.required_enforcement: Add ObservationPublication to the witness bound and two variants with controls (incomplete/extra/undeclared rule; inapplicable slice length != rule count); make variant reuse impossible (one witness fn per variant generated by the macro, or a test that counts trait methods from source and requires equality with ALL.len()).

The control project/identity/test.rs only opens the execution; it never evaluates or materializes.
